label: T1
title: Total equivalence of the evaluator.
reading: On every input, the Lean translation of the Rust decision function returns, without panicking or looping, exactly what the readable model returns.
text: Here \(x\) is the seven Rust inputs, and \(\mathsf{ok}\) is Aeneas's success, so neither a panic nor divergence. On every input the translated evaluator succeeds, never panicking or diverging, and its value denotes the model's result on the denoted inputs; this says nothing about allocation failure or compiled Wasm.

label: T2
title: Acceptance implies permission.
math:
\mathit{authorize}(R, \rho, (\vec c, \vec j, S, \ell, g)) = \rho'
\\
\qquad \implies \forall c \in \vec c.\ \exists r \in R.\ \mathit{allows}(r, c, S)
reading: If the decision function accepts a request, every call in it is allowed by some rule it was given, under the signers it was given.
text: If evaluation accepts, the selected rule set allows every supplied context for the signer list it was given. The theorem takes that list as an input; the account authenticates it (obligation O1).
hypotheses: The signer list is an input; the account authenticates it (O1)
evidence: [Chain.RuleSet.authorize_allowsAll](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/Chain.lean#L898) and [Extracted.authorize_allows_all](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/ExtractedAuthorize.lean#L79) · {{obj:PROVED · MODEL + TRANSLATION}}; the chosen rule as witness: [RuleSet.authorize_chosen](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/Authorize.lean#L208) · {{obj:PROVED · MODEL}}

label: T3
title: Signer accounting.
math:
\mathit{authorize}(R, \rho, (\vec c, \vec j, S, \ell, g)) = \rho'
\\
\qquad \implies \forall s \in S.\ \exists i.\ s \in \Sigma_{R_{j_i}}
\\
\mathit{signed}(r, S) \iff k_r \le |\Sigma_r \cap S|
\\
S \subseteq S' \land \mathit{allows}(R, c, S) \implies \mathit{allows}(R, c, S')
reading: Every signer of an accepted request belongs to a chosen rule; thresholds count distinct signers; more signers never turn an allow into a refusal.
text: Acceptance implies every supplied signer occurs in a chosen rule, and a threshold counts distinct listed identities. Adding identities preserves a rule's permission, though not whole-batch acceptance if an added identity is in no chosen rule.
hypotheses: The signer list is an input; the account authenticates it (O1)

label: T4
title: Attenuation narrows authority.
reading: A grant derived by attenuation steps allows no call its parent does not, under any signers; caps and expiry are outside this comparison.
text: Successful attenuation by the ten attenuation steps yields a rule set narrower than its parent: under any signers, every call the child allows, the parent allows. Repeated derivation preserves this relationship. *allows* reads no cap or expiry, so the steps that add or tighten them narrow only over runs ({{ref:stmt:trace-inclusion}}); parent and child keep separate records, and neither theorem bounds what they spend together. The account has no entry point that installs an attenuated grant at the pinned build.
hypotheses: Each derivation step is one of the ten attenuation steps and succeeds

label: T5
title: Trace inclusion.
reading: Every run a derived grant accepts from empty records, its parent accepts too, with rule numbers renumbered.
text: For a single successful derivation lineage, every accepted child history from empty records is accepted by the parent from empty records, with rule choices renumbered past dropped rules. Sibling histories are not covered. Here \(\vec a^{f}\) renumbers each choice \(j\) to \(f(j)\).

label: T6
title: Cap-window safety.
math:
\mathit{spent}_j(R, \varnothing, \vec a) = ((t_k, x_k))_{k=1}^{m}
\\
\quad \implies \forall L.\ \sum_{k:\ \max(0,\,L - P_j) < t_k \le L} x_k \;\le\; \lambda_j
\\
\quad \land\ \bigl((\forall a \in \vec a.\ \ell_a \ge 1) \implies
\\
\qquad \forall s.\ \sum_{k:\ s \le t_k < s + P_j} x_k \;\le\; \lambda_j\bigr)
reading: From an empty record, however the app times its payments, no window of P ledgers holds more than the limit in accepted charges.
text: From empty records, in any run, counting its accepted authorizations, the charges made to a capped rule with a non-negative limit after *L* − *P* and through *L* sum to at most its limit, for every ledger *L*. For the model, every *P* consecutive ledgers starting at ledger 1 or later are bounded too, with no ledger assumption; the *P* ledgers from 0 are bounded when every authorization is at ledger 1 or later. The translated form bounds the model's *spent* on the denoted inputs, which {{ref:stmt:total-equivalence-of-the-evaluator}} makes the translated run's charges.
hypotheses: Rule \(j\) of \(R\) has the cap \((\lambda_j, P_j)\) with \(\lambda_j \ge 0\); empty records. The second conjunct is proved for the model only. Without its hypothesis it fails from ledger 0: two charges of the limit at ledger 0 are both recorded (`Cap.period_ledger_zero`).
latex: From empty records, in any run, counting its accepted authorizations, the charges made to a capped rule with a non-negative limit after $L-P$ and through $L$ sum to at most its limit, for every ledger $L$. The model also bounds every $P$ consecutive ledgers that start at ledger~1 or later, and those from ledger~0 when no authorization is at ledger~0.

label: T7
title: Delegation-tree budgets.
math:
\mathit{valid}(T) \land (\forall n \in T.\ \mathit{spent}_n = 0)
\\
\quad \land\ \mathit{run}(T, \vec o) = (T', \mathit{log}) \land T'_a = n
\\
\qquad \implies \mathit{spentUnder}(T', \mathit{log}, a) \le \mathit{allowance}_n
reading: Spending beneath any node of a delegation tree never exceeds that node's allowance, even when its children's allowances add up to more than its own.
text: \(\mathit{valid}(T)\) says that every node's parent index is below its own and no allowance or spent amount is negative; \(\mathit{run}\) applies spends, delegations and refills in order, keeping the tree on a refused one and logging each successful spend; \(\mathit{spentUnder}(T', \mathit{log}, a)\) totals the logged spends made at or under node \(a\), and \(\mathit{allowance}_n\) is that node's allowance at the end. From a valid tree with nothing spent, spending beneath every node is at most its allowance, including when its children's allowances add up to more than its own. Allowances are lifetime totals, not windows, and refills raise them.
hypotheses: A valid tree with nothing spent

label: T8
title: Grant target containment.
math:
\mathit{lowerScoped}(d, A, X, g) = R
\\
\quad \land\ \mathit{Derives}(R, R')
\\
\quad \land\ \mathit{allows}(R', \mathsf{call}(C, f, \vec v), S)
\\
\qquad \implies C \neq A \;\land\; C \notin X
reading: No grant as lowered at install, nor any grant derived from one, allows a call to the account or its adopted recovery contracts.
text: \(\mathit{lowerScoped}(d, A, X, g)\) is the rule set the account installs for grant document \(d\) at address \(A\), with excluded set \(X\) and generation \(g\); it allows no call to \(A\) or to an element of \(X\), and attenuation preserves this. In the account, \(X\) is its adopted recovery controller and the zero-knowledge adapter and pool of its recovery configuration.
hypotheses: Lowering under address *A*, excluded set *X* and generation *g*; for the translation, each rule's argument conditions fit the evaluator's bounded vectors (`ArgsRoom`)

label: T9
title: The containment chain.
math:
\mathit{Valid}(d) \land \mathit{issue}(s, d) = R
\\
\quad \land\ \mathit{attenuateAll}(R, \vec\sigma) = R'
\\
\quad \land\ \mathit{authorize}(R', \rho, (\vec c, \vec j, S, \ell, g)) = \rho'
\\
\qquad \implies (\forall c \in \vec c.\ \mathit{Doc.allows}(d, A_s, c, S))
\\
\qquad \land\ (\forall \mathsf{call}(C, f, \vec v) \in \vec c.
\\
\qquad\qquad C \notin \mathit{excluded}(d_s, A_s))
\\
\qquad \land\ (\vec c \neq [\,] \implies g = g_s)
reading: A grant from a valid document, attenuated and accepted, allows only what the document allows, never the account or its excluded set, at its issuing generation.
text: Here \(s = (A_s, d_s, g_s)\) is the account state the grant is issued in, \(d_s\) its account document ({{ref:def:account-events}}). A grant issued from a valid grant document \(d\), then attenuated and accepted, allows only \(d\)'s actions and no call to the account or the excluded set at issue, and a nonempty batch is evaluated at the grant's issuing generation. The theorem assumes `Doc.Valid`; that Perch's validator accepts only valid documents is recorded as unproven (`{{fact:claim-perch-validation}}`). In the theorem, \(\mathit{excluded}(d_s, A_s)\) is the translated `excluded`; the account builds it from storage (O4), and because a controller can be adopted after a grant is installed, `__check_auth` rechecks each selected grant rule against the current set (`{{fact:claim-scoped-admin-change}}`).
latex: Here $s = (A_s, d_s, g_s)$ is the account state the grant is issued in, $d_s$ its account document. A grant issued from a valid grant document~$d$, then attenuated and accepted, allows only $d$'s actions and no call to the account or the excluded set at issue, and a nonempty batch is evaluated at the grant's issuing generation. The account builds the excluded set from its storage (O4) and rechecks it in \code{\_\_check\_auth} (\code{\fact{claim-scoped-admin-change}}).

label: T10
title: Recovery invalidation.
math:
\mathit{gen}(\mathit{run}(s, \vec e))
\\
\quad = \mathit{gen}(s) + \mathit{completions}(s, \vec e)
\\
\mathit{issue}(s, d) = R \;\land\; \mathit{attenuateAll}(R, \vec\sigma) = R'
\\
\quad \land\ \mathit{completions}(s, \vec e) > 0
\\
\quad \land\ g = \mathit{gen}(\mathit{run}(s, \vec e))
\\
\quad \land\ \mathit{authorize}(R', \rho, (\vec c, \vec j, S, \ell, g)) = \rho'
\\
\qquad \implies \vec c = [\,]
reading: After a completed recovery, no earlier grant, nor one derived from it, accepts a request with a call in it at the new generation.
text: In the account event model, the generation advances by exactly the number of completed recoveries, and a grant issued before one, or derived from such a grant, accepts no nonempty batch at the new generation. Administrative rules are generation-independent.
hypotheses: The authorization carries the account's current generation (O3)
evidence: [Document.Account.run_generation](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/Scoped.lean#L224); [Account.issued_stale](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/Scoped.lean#L251); [Account.chain_after_recovery](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/Scoped.lean#L321) · {{obj:PROVED · ACCOUNT MODEL}} (no Rust counterpart); stale-rule rejection: [Extracted.authorize_generation](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/ExtractedAuthorize.lean#L568) · {{obj:PROVED · MODEL + TRANSLATION}}

label: T11
title: Authorization-tree coverage.
math:
\mathsf{authorized}(A, f, \mathsf{entry}) \in \mathit{new}
\\
\quad \land\ \mathsf{checkRules}(R, S) \in \mathit{program}(A)
\\
\qquad \implies \mathit{allows}(R, f, S)
\\
\mathsf{checkAuth}(A, p, \sigma, \vec c) \in \mathit{new}
\\
\qquad \implies \vec c = \mathit{preorder}(p) \land \vec c \neq [\,]
reading: In the host model, every call an account's entry approves is allowed by the rules its `__check_auth` checks, and those see the whole tree.
text: Here \(\mathit{new}\) is the events a transaction's run appends. In the host model, every `require_auth` that an account's authorization entry satisfies is for a call that every rule set the modeled `__check_auth` checks allows, and `__check_auth` receives the entry's invocation tree in preorder, root first, so never an empty batch. The statement covers authorization by entry, not invoker authority, so an owner's `execute` falls outside it by construction. The modeled account is an abstract program checking the stateless `allows`, not Perch's shell. The model was tested against {{fact:host-model-tested-versions}} on {{fact:host-traces-generated}} traces it generated ({{fact:host-traces-named}} named, {{fact:host-traces-random}} random) and on {{fact:host-traces-transcribed}} traces transcribed from {{fact:host-tests-expressed}}, agreeing on every case it expresses ({{fact:host-cases-agreeing}} cases). It models CAP-0071 delegation between contract accounts; source-account credentials, classic Stellar-account signers and delegates, `require_auth_for_args`, `authorize_as_current_contract`, contract creation as a call, `require_auth` inside `__check_auth`, recording authorization, TTL and footprints are outside it, and the simulator host {{fact:soroban-env-host-sim}} was not tested.
hypotheses: Contract accounts; `require_auth` satisfied by an authorization entry
evidence: [Soroban.Tx.run_authorized_allowed](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/Soroban.lean#L705); [Tx.run_checkAuth_contexts](https://github.com/bitswell/soroban-rule-core/blob/cbabe594ae2df408991e825e56ddd618ea29541b/formal/RuleCore/Theorems/Soroban.lean#L717) · {{obj:PROVED · HOST MODEL}} (model tested against the host)
latex: Here $\mathit{new}$ is the events a transaction's run appends. In the host model, every \code{require\_auth} that an account's authorization entry satisfies is for a call that every rule set the modeled \code{\_\_check\_auth} checks allows, and \code{\_\_check\_auth} receives the entry's invocation tree in preorder, root first, so never an empty batch. Authorization by invoker, as in the owner's \code{execute}, is outside the statement, and the modeled account checks the stateless \textit{allows}, not Perch's shell. The model agreed with \fact{host-model-tested-versions} on every case it expresses, over \fact{host-traces-generated} generated and \fact{host-traces-transcribed} transcribed traces; Definition~\ref{def:host-run} and \S\ref{sec:unproved} list what it leaves out, and the simulator's host, \fact{soroban-env-host-sim}, was not tested.

label: T12
title: Lowering equivalence.
math:
\mathit{LowerRoom}(d) \implies \exists R.\ \mathit{lower}_{\mathrm{T}}(d, A) = \mathsf{ok}(R)
\\
\qquad \land\ \llbracket R \rrbracket = \mathit{lower}(\llbracket d \rrbracket, \llbracket A \rrbracket)
\\
\mathit{ArgsRoom}(d) \implies \exists y.
\\
\qquad \mathit{lowerScoped}_{\mathrm{T}}(d, A, X, g) = \mathsf{ok}(y)
\\
\qquad \land\ \llbracket y \rrbracket = \mathit{lowerScoped}(\llbracket d \rrbracket,
\\
\qquad\qquad \llbracket A \rrbracket, \llbracket X \rrbracket, \llbracket g \rrbracket)
reading: The translated lowering returns the model's rules; for a valid document they allow exactly what it allows, plus the recovery rule's call.
text: Translated `lower` returns the model's lowering when the document leaves room in its bounded vectors (`LowerRoom`), and translated `lower_scoped` does, refusals included, under the weaker `ArgsRoom`. For a valid document the lowered rules allow exactly what the document allows plus, when recovery is configured, every `apply_doc` call through the recovery rule, which the shell refuses outside a completion (tested; O8).
hypotheses: `LowerRoom` for `lower`, `ArgsRoom` for `lower_scoped`; `Doc.Valid` for the semantic part

label: T13
title: Canonical identity.
reading: Two different modeled documents never have the same canonical bytes.
text: Perch's canonical encoding is injective on the modeled document type; hash identity then holds up to SHA-256 collisions, an assumption outside the theorem. The theorem is about a Lean emitter written to match Perch's Rust `canon.rs` and linked to it by golden fixtures and fuzzing, not extraction; JSON parsing and compiler correctness need separate assurance, and no theorem connects this encoding to rule-core's document type. The CANON version is not part of the hashed bytes, so a `doc_hash` is read under the identity the account reports (`capabilities().doc_identity`); three domain separations are proven: `configPreimage_ne_emitDoc`, `rulePreimage_ne_configPreimage` and `rulePreimage_ne_emitDoc` (rule, recovery-configuration and document preimages are pairwise distinct).

label: P1
title: From the evaluator to the account.
reading: If the account meets obligations O1–O8, each call a grant rule approves is allowed by the grant's document, calls neither the account nor its excluded set, and stops after a recovery.
text: Under obligations O1–O8, {{ref:stmt:total-equivalence-of-the-evaluator}} with `RuleSet.authorize_chosen`, the per-rule forms of {{ref:stmt:grant-target-containment}} and {{ref:stmt:the-containment-chain}} (`Doc.lowerScoped_contract`, `Doc.lowerScoped_allows`), and `authorize_generation` ({{ref:stmt:recovery-invalidation}}) give, for each context whose selected rule belongs to a grant: the context is allowed by the grant's source document, calls neither the account nor its excluded set, and is refused after a completed recovery.
hypotheses: Obligations O1–O8. O1, O3, O4 and O6–O8 are tested, O2 is argued and tested, and O5, that compiler outputs satisfy `Doc.Valid`, is unproven (`{{fact:claim-perch-validation}}`); every grant rule satisfies `ArgsRoom` (assumed, `rule.lower-room`); the account's Wasm, built by rustc {{fact:rustc-perch}}, computes what the translation computes (trusted; nothing checks it)
evidence: Argued from the theorems above and the obligations; not mechanized · {{obj:ARGUED}}
